feed.heading: Who he was
life: Born of noble parents in Thessalonica, Demetrius rose to command all the Roman forces in Thessaly and to serve as Proconsul of Hellas. Yet he put his faith before every honor, and by word and example brought many pagans to Christ.

Denounced to the Emperor Maximian, he was thrown into a cell beneath the baths. With his blessing the young Nestor slew the mighty Lyaios in the arena; then soldiers killed Demetrius with spears. Fragrant myrrh flowed from his body, healing many.
feed.intercession: Holy Great-martyr Demetrius, pray to God for us.
feed.caption:
Today (October 26, New Calendar) the Church keeps the feast of the Holy Greatmartyr Demetrius of Thessalonica.

Born of noble parents, Demetrius became commander of all the Roman forces in Thessaly and Proconsul of Hellas. Despite these worldly honors he put his Christian faith before all, and by his words and example brought many pagans to Christ.

When the Emperor Maximian came to Thessalonica, Demetrius was denounced and cast into a cell. He blessed the young Nestor, who cried out “God of Demetrius, help me!” and overcame the mighty Lyaios in the arena. The Emperor then sent soldiers who killed Demetrius with their spears.

Fragrant myrrh flowed from the Martyr’s body after his death, healing many of the sick. For many centuries he has been a patron saint of Thessalonica.
